name: Spotify
one_liner: Instant in development mode for up to 5 allowlisted users (owner needs Premium); public access needs Extended Quota Mode, which since May 2025 is only for registered organizations with at least 250k MAU.
difficulty_reason: Testing takes minutes, but Extended Quota Mode is gated on business criteria (organization, launched service, 250k+ MAU, key markets) that most agent builders cannot meet, and the Developer Policy restricts AI ingestion and voice-assistant style control.
time_to_first_test: 10-20 minutes (inferred; requires the app owner to have Spotify Premium)
time_to_production: Not reachable for most teams; eligible organizations wait an unpublished time for partner approval, then up to 6 weeks of app review

approval.required_for: Any use beyond 5 allowlisted Spotify users per Client ID (development mode). Extended Quota Mode removes the allowlist and raises rate limits.
approval.who_reviews: Spotify partner team (Partner Application form, company email only), then Spotify's app review team via the Quota extension Request tab in the Developer Dashboard
approval.typical_wait: App review: Spotify states 'can take up to six weeks'. Partner Application form review time: not published.
approval.cost: Free to apply (no fee published). Development mode requires the app owner to keep a paid Spotify Premium subscription.

account_prerequisites: Spotify account with an active Premium subscription for the app owner (development mode stops working if Premium lapses)
Acceptance of the Spotify Developer Terms (v10, effective 15 May 2025)
For Extended Quota Mode: legally registered business or organization (individuals not accepted since 15 May 2025)
For Extended Quota Mode: active, launched service with at least 250k MAUs, available in key Spotify markets, commercially viable
For Extended Quota Mode: application sent from a company email address
Privacy policy describing how you access, use, process and disclose user data (Developer Policy requirement)
Website URL for the app settings

steps.title: Log in to the Developer Dashboard with a Premium account
steps.detail: Use the Spotify account that will own the app. Development mode apps only work while this owner has Premium.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click Create an App, enter App Name and App Description (shown to users on the consent screen), tick the Developer Terms of Service box and click Create. Up to 25 apps per developer account as of July 2026.

steps.title: Set website and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add a Website URL and one or more Redirect URIs. Use HTTPS; for local testing use http://127.0.0.1:PORT or http://[::1]:PORT. localhost is rejected. Redirect URIs must match exactly (only loopback IP literals may vary the port). If using Composio, paste the redirect URI Composio shows for your custom auth config.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Store the client secret in a secret manager. Use the authorization code flow (with PKCE for public clients); implicit grant is deprecated.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Request only the scopes your agent needs (for example user-read-playback-state, playlist-modify-private). The Developer Policy says to only request data needed to operate your app.

steps.title: Allowlist test users
steps.detail: Settings > Users Management > Add new user, enter name and Spotify email. Max 5 users per app. Non-allowlisted users can log in but API calls return 403.

steps.title: Build against the development mode endpoint set
steps.detail: Since the February 2026 changes, development mode apps lose batch endpoints, browse/new releases, artist top tracks, other users' profiles/playlists, several response fields (for example email and product on GET /me), and search limit max drops to 10. Extended Quota Mode apps are unaffected.

steps.title: Check Extended Quota eligibility before planning a public launch
steps.detail: You need: registered business, launched service, at least 250k MAUs, presence in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, adherence to terms. If you do not meet these, plan the product around the 5-user cap or drop Spotify.

steps.title: Submit the Partner Application form
steps.detail: Submit from a company email via the Google Form linked on the Quota modes page.

steps.title: Request the quota extension in the dashboard
steps.detail: Only after the Partner Application is approved: app > Settings > Quota extension Request tab, fill in the 4-step questionnaire and Submit. Status shows 'Sent'. Feedback arrives by email; review can take up to six weeks.

nuances: Development mode cap is 5 authenticated users per Client ID (was 25 before Feb/Mar 2026); apps that already had more than 5 users were grandfathered.
Development mode requires the app owner to have Spotify Premium; if Premium lapses the app stops working until resubscribed.

Since July 2026 a developer can create up to 25 Client IDs, but development mode quotas are counted per developer account, so multiple Client IDs share one quota. Splitting users across apps does not raise throughput.
Exceeding the development mode quota returns 429 with reason QUOTA_EXCEEDED; this is separate from normal rate limits.

Redirect URIs: HTTPS required except loopback; use 127.0.0.1 or [::1], never localhost. Loopback IP literals may be registered without a port and the port added at request time (RFC 8252). Custom schemes such as com.example://callback still work per the Feb 2025 blog examples.
Rules enforced for apps created from 9 April 2025; all existing clients were expected to migrate by November 2025.
Implicit grant (response_type=token) is deprecated; use authorization code, with PKCE for public clients.
Access tokens last 1 hour. A refresh token might not be returned on every refresh; keep using the old one when absent and store the new one when present.

February 2026 changes removed many endpoints and fields for development mode apps (batch GETs, browse categories, new releases, artist top tracks, GET /users/{id}, user email/country/product). Endpoint changes for existing integrations were postponed on 9 March 2026, but the Premium, user-cap and Client ID rules went ahead.
Playlist contents (items) are only returned for playlists the user owns or collaborates on in development mode.
When a user disconnects, delete their Spotify personal data; the Developer Terms appendix sets a five-day deadline.
App Name and Description are shown on the consent screen; with your own app the user sees your name, not Composio's.

blockers.blocker: Extended Quota Mode only accepts organizations with a launched service and at least 250k MAUs (since 15 May 2025).
blockers.how_to_proceed: If you do not qualify, ship only to up to 5 allowlisted users per app (internal tool, personal agent), or remove Spotify from the public launch. Do not rely on many dev-mode apps: quota is pooled per developer account and the policy intent is non-commercial use.

blockers.blocker: Development Mode is for non-commercial, individual use per the Feb 2026 announcement.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Do not run a paid or public agent product on a development mode app; treat it as a sandbox only.

blockers.blocker: Developer Policy bans voice assistants that control Spotify, ingesting Spotify Content into an ML or AI model, and analytics/user profiling built from Spotify data.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Get a legal read on whether your agent's design (for example, passing track metadata to an LLM, natural-language playback control) is allowed before applying. Keep Spotify data out of training and logs that feed models.

blockers.blocker: App owner must hold Spotify Premium.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Use a company-paid Premium account as the app owner so the app does not break when a personal subscription lapses.
Use http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback for local tests and HTTPS for deployed callbacks.

agent_can_do: Generate valid redirect URIs (HTTPS for production, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] for local) and check they match exactly between dashboard and code
Pick the minimal scope list for the agent's tools
Implement authorization code + PKCE flow and refresh-token handling (1 hour access tokens, optional refresh token rotation)
Audit code for endpoints and fields removed for development mode apps in Feb 2026 and migrate to /me/library and /playlists/{id}/items
Draft a privacy policy that covers data access, use, disclosure, and 5-day deletion on disconnect
Draft answers for the Partner Application form and the 4-step quota extension questionnaire
Check the app against Developer Policy prohibitions (AI ingestion, voice control, business use, games, mixing)
Check via the Composio API whether composio_managed_auth_schemes includes Spotify OAuth (currently it does not)
you_must_do: Own a Spotify account with active Premium and log in to the Developer Dashboard
Accept the Developer Terms of Service
Copy and store the client secret securely
Add each tester's name and Spotify email to the allowlist
Confirm the business meets Extended Quota criteria (registered entity, 250k+ MAU, launched service) and submit the Partner Application from a company email
Submit the quota extension request and answer reviewer emails
Get legal sign-off that the agent use case complies with the Developer Policy and Terms
composio_note: Composio does not offer managed OAuth for Spotify. The Spotify toolkit page shows 'Composio-managed OAuth not available' and its FAQ says to create your own OAuth app in the Spotify Developer Dashboard. So you must register a Spotify app, then create a custom auth config in Composio with your Client ID and Client Secret and add Composio's redirect URI to the app. Your app's quota mode applies: without Extended Quota Mode only 5 allowlisted users can connect, and some of the toolkit's 88 tools (for example batch gets, new releases, artist top tracks, other users' playlists) call endpoints Spotify removed for development mode apps in Feb 2026.

verification.method: Read official docs listed in sources; no provider account created
verified: Development mode allows up to 5 authenticated users per app, each added to an allowlist
Development mode requires the app owner to have Spotify Premium
Extended Quota Mode accepts only organizations since 15 May 2025, with at least 250k MAUs and a launched service
Partner Application must come from a company email; dashboard quota extension request follows approval
App review can take up to six weeks
Up to 25 Client IDs per developer since July 2026; development mode quota is pooled per developer account
localhost redirect URIs are not allowed; HTTPS required except loopback IP literals
Developer Policy bans AI/ML ingestion of Spotify Content, voice assistants, business-targeted products
Composio does not provide managed OAuth for Spotify
inferred: Time to first test of 10-20 minutes, based on the short app creation form
An LLM agent that passes Spotify Content to a model may conflict with the 'ingest Spotify Content into a machine learning or AI model' clause; Spotify does not define this for agents
Some Composio Spotify tools will fail for development mode apps created after 11 Feb 2026 because they call removed endpoints
No application fee, since none is mentioned in the docs
could_not_verify: Review time for the Partner Application form (not published)
Which markets count as 'key Spotify markets'
Exact development mode quota bucket limits ('subject to change', not published)
Whether postponed endpoint removals for pre-Feb-2026 dev mode apps have since been rescheduled
The 5-day deletion clause was read through a summarizing fetch tool, not a raw page dump
corrections: Common advice says development mode allows 25 users; since 11 Feb 2026 (new apps) and 9 Mar 2026 (existing apps) the cap is 5, and the owner needs Premium
Common advice says anyone can request a quota extension from the dashboard; since 15 May 2025 only organizations with 250k+ MAU qualify, and a Partner Application form must be approved first
Common advice says one Client ID per developer (Feb 2026 rule); this rose to 25 in July 2026, but quota is shared across them
http://localhost redirect URIs no longer work; use http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1]
Implicit grant tutorials are outdated; the flow is deprecated
Development mode apps no longer receive email, country or product from GET /me, so do not rely on Spotify for user email
Composio cannot be used as a shortcut around Spotify's app review: there is no Composio-managed Spotify app
